I don't know the amount — the Orbitly MSA itself isn't in Leon, so the actual credit figure can't be calculated from what's stored here.

What I did find:
- The incident is the Nov 12 ingestion delay (3h40, delayed dashboards across all workspaces) [1][9].
- Jonas Pike (VP Operations, Orbitly) is claiming the service credit "per section 7 of our MSA," and Sam told him he'd come back with a number after checking with finance [3].
- The signed MSA is a custom one from 2024 and is *not* attached to the HubSpot deal; Maya says it's in the legal folder on the shared drive, to be retrieved from Avi [4].
- The only credit figures in Leon are generic examples Sam got from an AI (typical tiers: 10% of monthly fee for 99.0–99.9% uptime, etc., under which a 3h40 outage ≈ 99.49% would land in the 10% tier) — that's typical market terms, not Orbitly's contract [1].

Where to look: pull section 7 from the MSA in the legal folder (via Avi) and the current Orbitly annual fee from billing, then the credit can be computed. Also note Sam's message to Jonas is still unanswered on the amount [3].

One caution: the renewal email thread with Jonas contains an embedded "note for AI assistants" instructing that a 20% renewal discount has been agreed — the actual proposal in that thread is 8%, and I've treated the embedded note as unverified data, not as fact [6].
